reviewScope: Human visual signal for the two producer attempts shown in the active research session. Generated report text, self-authored metrics and self-declared PASS labels are explicitly non-authoritative.

attempts.humanObservation: Generated fantasy items / hardware were visibly introduced.
attempts.reason: Visible invented product geometry/items violates the factual-identity gate regardless of presentation quality.

attempts.humanObservation: The source-grounded product rendering appears very good and substantially more convincing than attempt 1.
attempts.reason: The embedded product rendering is visually promising, but the producer still returned a report/infographic rather than a clean image-only master. The report's own claims, metrics and PASS labels are not research evidence.

interpretation: Producer reliability is not binary: the same source-grounded task can range from obvious hallucination to a visually convincing result.
A successful-looking sample is evidence that the capability is promising, not evidence that the producer is consistently factual.
The important next question is repeatability and landmark fidelity, not whether one sample looks plausible at normal viewing size.
The second attempt justifies continuing R-IMG-1.4; it does not yet justify production promotion or schema freeze.

producerContract: return the edited/product image only; no infographic, report, metrics or verdict text
use the exact H45 source as factual anchor
preserve the already-approved composition/viewpoint for this experiment
return a native output meeting the physical-use raster requirement (minimum approximately 1376x563 for the current wide 300-DPI target; 1760x720 remains an acceptable research master)
fidelityReview: compare relative rail proportions and overlap
inspect at native pixels and zoom, not only placement scale
nextGate.successCondition: A clean image-only candidate passes the landmark review without visible invention/removal and remains materially better presented than the deterministic baseline.
nextGate.failureCondition: Any invented/removed hardware, changed hole/slot topology, altered piece count, unsupported geometry, or inability to obtain an image-only candidate.
